title: A Demonstration of Correlation of Correlation Analysis
text:
Introduction

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

import seaborn as sns

sns.set_context('talk')

df = sns.load_dataset('flights')

RQ: Do the number of flights increase over the years?
An advid traveler is looking to become a history buff and see if there is any relationship to the amount of flights over the years. They plan to look at the seaborn dataset flights that has a total of 144 trips.


Literature Review


Methods
Given that we have two coloumns of continuous data (year and passenger) we will evalute this relationship using simple correlation analysis and also a scatter plot. These two methods are classic and tradtional starting points when evaluting data like these.


Results

corr_val = df['year'].corr(df['passengers'])

narative = "a very strong negative correaltion"

if corr_val > 0.8: 
    narrative = "a very strong positive correlation"
elif corr_val > .4:
    narrative = "a moderate postive correaltion"
elif corr_val > 0:
    narrative = "a positve but weak correlation"
elif corr_val > -.4:
    narrative = "a moderate negative correaltion"

Using the classic simple Pearson correlation approach these data produce a correltation coefficent of 0.9218238352924206, as such, given this result, we conclude that the relationship is a very strong positive correlation.
